text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Kuwait's press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Government objects to the holding extraordinary parliament sessions on Saturdays. Kuwait's parliament, which holds weekly meetings on Tuesdays, wants added sessions to discuss the government agenda.
- Foreign Minister Sheikh Sabah al-Ahmad al-Sabah receives messages from Bahraini and Saudi Arabian counterparts.
- More rain and drop in temperature at night, weather forecasters say.
- No taxes on industrial construction, no favouritism for foreign investors over Kuwaiti nationals, Commerce and Industry Minister Jassem al-Mudaf says.
- Relatives of Central Prison inmates protest against new measures. A wired partition has been erected at the visiting area.
- Parliamentary panel investigates the fate of 1,200 Kuwaiti workers at the Ports Authority in case of privatisation.
- Electric power may be cut off if bills are not paid, Electricity Ministry says.
- Parliament's human rights panel sets focus on prison issues.
